questionText:
Read the following excerpt on structural transformations under colonialism:

Colonialism introduced far-reaching structural changes in the Indian subcontinent. British economic policies were designed to serve the industrial interests of the metropolitan power. As Britain underwent its Industrial Revolution, the British state systematically dismantled India's world-renowned artisanal handloom and handicraft sectors. Indian raw materials (such as raw cotton and jute) were extracted and exported cheaply to British factories, while finished British machine-made textiles from Manchester flooded the Indian market free of duty. This process, termed 'de-industrialisation' by economic historians, caused massive unemployment among traditional weavers and artisans. Deprived of their urban livelihoods and royal patronage, millions of displaced artisans were forced to migrate back into villages, creating acute pressure on agricultural land. Concurrently, the colonial administration developed coastal port cities like Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras to facilitate this imperial trade, while historic inland trading hubs and royal capitals suffered severe decline.

Question: What was the direct consequence of the destruction of urban handicrafts on the rural agrarian economy?

options.text: All agricultural land was turned into wildlife sanctuaries

options.text: Villagers abandoned farming and moved into high-rise luxury apartment blocks
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

options.text: Peasants received free mechanised tractors from the British government
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.
